# 2 Baruch Chapter 13 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 13:2 — "endure tribulation" vs. "hold on through suffering"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "able-to-endure-tribulation" | Literal; "tribulation" as standard eschatological term |
| LOGOS | "able to endure tribulation" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "can hold on through suffering" | "Hold on" for "endure"; "suffering" for "tribulation" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Endure tribulation" is the established phrase in Jewish and early Christian eschatological texts. "Tribulation" carries apocalyptic specificity that "suffering" lacks.

---

## 13:9 — Lamp metaphor

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-lamp that-shines-within-a-house shall-be-extinguished when-it-is-no-longer-needed" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "a lamp that shines within a house shall be extinguished when it is no longer needed" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "A lamp that lights a room goes out when it is no longer needed" | "Lights a room" for "shines within a house"; "goes out" for "shall be extinguished" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Shines within a house" is the fuller Syriac expression, matching the house/household imagery. "Shall be extinguished" is more deliberate than "goes out."

---

## 13:12 — "the law go forth" — Isa 2:3 allusion

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "out-of-Zion-shall-the-Law-go-forth" | Literal with capital; Isa 2:3 allusion |
| LOGOS | "out of Zion shall the law go forth" | Formal, preserves allusion |
| PNEUMA | "from Zion the Law will go out" | "Will go out" for "shall go forth"; preposition variation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Shall go forth" preserves the prophetic/declarative register of the Isaiah quotation. "Go out" is too casual for a scriptural citation.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
